transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-03 16:00 PDT | Duration: 63m | Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (Partner Lead) + VeroScale team (Daniel, Elena, Marcus, TJ, Asha)

Summary (auto): Aligning on go-to-market surge for North America mid-market accounts; legal clearance gating items identified; agreed to run a short 2-week benchmark and collect security docs.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick roll call?
00:08 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Daniel here, head of alliances at VeroScale.
00:11 Speaker 3 (Elena): Elena, legal counsel.
00:13 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Marcus, GTM lead.
00:15 Speaker 5 (Marco): Marco Diaz from Redwood, solutions eng.
00:18 Speaker 6 (Priya): Priya from partnerships, hi all.
00:21 Speaker 7 (TJ): TJ, sales ops.
00:23 Speaker 8 (Asha): Asha, solutions arch.
00:25 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Awesome. Agenda — quick pipeline snapshot, scope for a two-week benchmark, legal redlines and security checklist, co-sell motion and revenue split, and next steps. If anything else, call it out.

02:00 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Quick context — we have a marketing push next month across mid-market verticals, about 120 target accounts. We want Redwood in our co-sell offer, fast. Not looking for a long POC if possible, want a quick bench to validate latency and cost numbers before commit.

02:27 Speaker 5 (Marco): Cool. Baseline question: are these mostly cloud-native stacks or on-prem heavy? The routing and private deployment asks change the approach.

02:36 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Mostly cloud — AWS, some GCP. But 20% have infosec demands like VPC peering or strict data residency.

02:49 Speaker 5 (Marco): Got it. For the 80% hosted accounts we can do our hosted API with region routing; for the 20% we should plan dedicated capacity or private options. That will impact unit economics.

03:10 Speaker 3 (Elena): Legal here — our vendor risk team will need SOC2 Type II evidence, encryption-at-rest proofs, key management details, and an indemnity clause that aligns with our policy. We also have some customers that require data to be stored in country X.

03:28 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Noted. We have a public SOC2 pack and a gated security packet. I can share a link after the call. We also support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments — that covers a lot of KMS asks.

03:45 Speaker 3 (Elena): Please share the vendor questionnaire answers, that'll speed the security review.

04:02 Speaker 6 (Priya): On the co-sell motion — VeroScale handles initial outbound and discovery, Redwood provides technical enablement and joint account playbooks. For net-new logo opportunities we propose a 60/40 split in favor of the seller on closed ARR but happy to table that. Do you have any internal rules about splits?

04:26 Speaker 1 (Sophie): We are flexible — we typically do a partner-friendly split for early-stage co-sells. We'll put a draft proposal in the deck.

04:35 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Can we get a rough SLA on latency? Some of our customers complained about lag with competitor endpoints, which slowed demos.

04:45 Speaker 5 (Marco): For typical generation workloads at 1k tokens, our hosted p95 latency is ~210-260ms in NA regions, depending on model variant; Dedicated can drop that to ~140-180ms. But there's tradeoffs with batching and cost.

05:05 Speaker 8 (Asha): Is that number for Redwood's latest runtime build? We need the perf kit for our benchmarks to be reproducible.

05:13 Speaker 5 (Marco): Yes that's with the 2027.3 runtime, but I'll capture exact model specs and kernel settings in the test plan.

05:22 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Good. We also care about cost per 1k tokens because that affects our packaging and pricing. Is there a recommended placement when cost is sensitive?

05:34 Speaker 1 (Sophie): For cost-sensitive customers, our Optimize recommendations often suggest a smaller model + quantization profile and aggressive prefix caching for templated chat flows. We can run a quick cost simulation against a sample prompt set you share.

06:00 Speaker 7 (TJ): How long to stand up a dedicated pool for those 20% accounts?

06:07 Speaker 5 (Marco): If it's reserved capacity, standard lead time is 2–3 weeks for provisioning in NA — less if we can reallocate burst capacity. For private deployments/VPC peering, it depends on customer's network readiness — often 3–6 weeks.

06:28 Speaker 4 (Marcus): For go-to-market timing, our campaign launch is 2027-05-17. We need a go/no-go decision by 2027-05-12. Can you commit to the benchmark and security artifacts before that?

06:40 Speaker 1 (Sophie): We'll prioritize — Sophie to share deck and SOC2 pack within 48 hours, Marco will scope a 2-week benchmark plan starting 2027-05-06 assuming access provisioned.

07:02 Speaker 3 (Elena): On the indemnity and data residency — some of our customers require explicit language limiting cross-border transfer. We may need a narrow subprocesser list. Is Redwood open to carving out a subprocessors section?

07:22 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Yes, we can surface subprocessors and discuss carve-outs. For enterprise Private installs we can avoid that by keeping data in-custody.

07:34 Speaker 2 (Daniel): On sales ops — we'll need a joint lead list and qualifying criteria; TJ here will own lead routing.

07:45 Speaker 7 (TJ): Route format — we'd like an API or CSV with lead metadata and initial intent signal, ideally pushed to our Salesforce instance. How does Redwood want to receive leads?

07:58 Speaker 1 (Sophie): We can integrate via a webhook or send a CSV; we also have a partner portal that can push leads. I'll have Priya follow up with an integration spec.

08:20 Speaker 6 (Priya): I'm on that. Also propose a joint webinar week-of-campaign to create pipeline acceleration.

08:30 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Perfect. Back to security — Elena will share the vendor questionnaire now?

08:36 Speaker 3 (Elena): I'll share the template, but we need answers back by 2027-05-10. Also can you confirm whether Redwood retains logs and for how long? Some customers require 90-day retention max.

08:51 Speaker 5 (Marco): Log retention is configurable per-customer in Dedicated/Private. For hosted, standard logs are 365 days but we can set retention policies for co-sell accounts if agreed.

09:05 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Competition question — we had one client mention Aurelia AI's similar co-sell play. How do you differentiate on reliability and ops?

09:14 Speaker 5 (Marco): Two big differentiators: unified runtime that gives consistent latency across modes, and built-in fallback policies so if capacity in one region or model variant drops, requests auto-reroute to a compatible variant. Also deep observability per-token for cost tracing — helps with pricing transparency.

09:36 Speaker 4 (Marcus): For sales decks, we need a one-pager that succinctly explains these points and example TCO comparisons vs. Aurelia.

09:47 Speaker 1 (Sophie): We'll include a TCO table + example tradeoffs (dedicated vs hosted) in the deck.

10:05 Speaker 8 (Asha): Technical deep-dive: during the benchmark we want KV cache behavior and how stateful chat is handled across restarts. If we have a short session expiry, will the performance numbers be affected?

10:20 Speaker 5 (Marco): Good call — KV cache warmup matters. We'll include cold-start and warmed metrics. Also outline guidance for checkpointing KV cache for private deployments.

10:35 Speaker 3 (Elena): Also need to flag any third-party telemetry or analytics sent to external services. Our vendor team flags anything that leaves the control plane.

10:45 Speaker 1 (Sophie): We log telemetry for performance monitoring; raw customer prompts are not sent to third parties. We can provide a telemetry mapping doc.

11:02 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Let's talk numbers — target is to convert at least 8–12 accounts in quarter 3 from this surge, conservative ARR per account $70k ARR. We want a clear path to proof for those accounts.

11:20 Speaker 6 (Priya): Recommend a pilot cohort of 6 accounts with mixed profiles (3 easy deploy hosted, 2 dedicated, 1 private). That gives representative coverage.

11:33 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Agreed. We'll propose the cohort list and runbooks. We'll also include win criteria: p95 latency under 300ms for hosted, model cost under $0.40 per 1k tokens effective for typical prompts, and successful SSO and SAML test for private accounts.

12:00 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Legal aside — indemnity caps. We typically push for mutual caps. Would Redwood accept mutual?

12:09 Speaker 1 (Sophie): We can discuss mutual caps; I'll flag our legal team and loop in Redwood legal if we get to the contract stage.

12:20 Speaker 3 (Elena): If we move fast on the vendor questionnaire and redlines, we can probably clear legal by 2027-05-11 which meets our 5/12 gating date.

12:33 Speaker 7 (TJ): Logistics — who will own customer-facing enablement assets? We need battlecards and template emails.

12:41 Speaker 6 (Priya): Redwood will produce technical battlecards; VeroScale will produce verticalized email templates. We'll coordinate the joint assets repo.

12:55 Speaker 1 (Sophie): I'll upload a shared folder and invite everyone: co-sell deck, security pack, benchmark plan. Links: partnership playbook: https://drive.redwood.com/partnerships/veroscale-playbook (access: partner-only), SOC2 & security pack: https://portal.redwood.com/security/veroscale-supply (gated).

13:20 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Quick pricing question — how do you recommend we structure the bundle in the offering? Monthly subscription + per-usage token surcharge or fully usage-based?

13:32 Speaker 1 (Sophie): For mid-market, a hybrid approach works well: base subscription for predictability + usage component for overages. We'll put examples in the deck tied to TCO.

13:50 Speaker 3 (Elena): Final note from legal — we'll need to confirm data residency options for specific countries; I'll enumerate which customers have that requirement in the vendor questionnaire.

14:03 Speaker 5 (Marco): Noted. We'll call out the Private/VPC path in the runbook and what lead time is needed.

14:20 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Recap — action items: Sophie to send deck + security docs in 48h; Marco to scope benchmark plan and perf targets; Elena to return vendor Q by 5/10; Priya to draft joint outreach and webinar schedule; TJ to work on lead routing spec. We aim to reach go/no-go on 2027-05-12.

14:45 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Sounds good. Any final questions?

14:52 Speaker 8 (Asha): One more — will we have access to a sandbox account for the bench?

14:57 Speaker 5 (Marco): Yes we'll provision a partner sandbox — need contact details. Sophie, can you capture the provisioning owner after?

15:05 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Will do. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and docs.

15:15 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Thanks all.

15:20 Speaker 3 (Elena): Bye.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts referenced: partnership playbook link (partner only), security pack (gated), benchmark sheet: https://drive.redwood.com/benchmarks/veroscale-bench-2027.xlsx

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels (Speaker X), some words may be transcribed incorrectly (e.g., GTM -> GT M).
